findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no no-arg version exists in UsernameForm or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator — the only definition is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), which has a different signature and is not visible to UsernameForm, causing a compile failure that breaks the entire PR build.

[ADVISORY] UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null, inverting the original null-user condition, so fillContextForm is never invoked from UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate on the initial no-user login page; this breaks conditional passkey login for unidentified users and causes the new tests (passwordLoginWithExternalKey, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication) asserting the webauth form element on the first login screen to fail.

[ADVISORY] UsernamePasswordForm.java:117 — the moved webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) call now executes unconditionally in authenticate(), duplicating the fillContextForm invocation already made via challenge(context, ...) on the normal first-render path, doubling per-render work (auth session notes, WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean credential lookup) and side effects.

[ADVISORY] AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:222 — badPasswordHandler now delegates to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError which reads the auth note inline, duplicating the isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth helper's predicate logic in the same class hierarchy, risking silent divergence between the two readers when the flag storage changes.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate: the new !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() branch has no test assertion verifying which branch executed — PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication passes identically whether the username form was rendered or silently skipped, so a regression in the skip condition ships undetected; the test never asserts loginPage.assertCurrent() or presence/absence of the username field between the re-auth request and appPage.assertCurrent()

[ADVISORY] Missing test coverage for re-authentication of a user with no passkey credential while realm passkeys policy is enabled — the only 'user without passkey' test sets WebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled to FALSE, so the case the UsernameForm change alters (passkeys enabled, context.getUser() != null, zero webauthn credentials) is never exercised; a password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm is forced back through a username form with unknown rendering state instead of skipping to the password step

[ADVISORY] UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate: inverting the gate from isPasskeysEnabled() to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) drops the first-factor (user == null) fillContextForm call, so combined username/password flows lose conditional-UI setup on the initial login page; no test asserts webauthn autocomplete/conditional-UI presence on the initial page where user is null, making a regression breaking first-login passkey login via the combined form invisible

[BUG] UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no such method exists in the diff or its parent class AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator; the method exists only on sibling class UsernamePasswordForm, so the class does not compile and the passkeys re-authentication behavior does not ship

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: the guard in UsernameForm now forces the username form to be shown during every re-authentication in passkeys-enabled realms, but no test exercises UsernameForm itself; the interplay of hasLinkedBrokers with the new condition has zero coverage, so regressions (e.g., broker re-auth users seeing an unexpected username form) ship silently

[ADVISORY] Parallel hand-maintained gating: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) in UsernamePasswordForm re-implements the passkeys-available check already owned by WebAuthnAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled(), and the no-arg variant in UsernameForm is a second divergent copy; future conditions must be updated in multiple places, risking drift between flows — the gate should live in one place per the single-source-of-truth rule

[ADVISORY] Naming/scope mismatch: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is documented for the username-password form error path but is also invoked on the WebAuthn conditional-UI error challenge, setting USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a form outside its specified contract, so template changes to USERNAME_HIDDEN will silently affect the webauthn error page

[ADVISORY] Public-surface widening: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is changed from protected to public solely so a util class in a different package can read it, making an internal auth-note key part of the permanent public API and making future renames/restructuring a breaking change for out-of-tree subclasses

[ADVISORY] Test smell in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest: the 'webauthn button not present' assertions use try/catch with fail() as control flow, swallowing any exception (including NoSuchElementException) as a pass; these assertions can pass for the wrong reason and mask regressions, and should use Assert.assertThrows which is already used elsewhere in the same PR

[BUG] UsernameForm.java:47 — skip condition now gates on realm passkey policy instead of the user's actual credentials; a user with no WebAuthn credential in a passkey-enabled realm re-authenticating regresses from 'skip to password' to 're-enter username', contradicting the re-auth UX contract (USERNAME_HIDDEN) this PR preserves, since WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm bails out early offering them nothing for the extra step

[ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.java:132 — util package statically imports a constant from browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, inverting the dependency direction between the util layer and browser-authenticator layer; the constant was promoted from protected to public solely for this import, and the pattern will grow the public surface with every shared note name — the note name should live in (or be passed from) the util/contract layer both read

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.java:47 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments but the only definition added in the diff is the protected (UserModel user) overload in sibling class UsernamePasswordForm; if no zero-arg overload exists this does not compile, and if it does, the two same-named predicates in sibling classes with different semantics is a naming collision that will mislead future editors and enable copy-paste bugs with divergent null-user handling

[ADVISORY] PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey — coverage gap: no test exercises re-authentication through the separate UsernameForm execution for a user with no WebAuthn credential while the realm has passkeys enabled, precisely the case whose behavior changed in UsernameForm.authenticate; future tweaks or regressions to the skip condition would pass CI while silently changing re-auth UX in production

[BUG] UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (lines 113-116): the original code set up WebAuthn data on the initial login page when user was not selected, but the diff inverts this so fillContextForm is only called when the user is already selected; the conditional-UI autofill setup for the anonymous first page is silently reversed, so the first username/password page no longer emits conditional-UI WebAuthn attributes and users lose browser passkey autofill on the initial page.

[ADVISORY] PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 197-207): a previously accepted assertion that passkeys must be hidden on the username/password page once the user is identified is flipped to require the webauth form present, reversing an accepted behavioral constraint without evidence the spec owner signed off.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm (line 47): the re-auth skip condition changed from a per-user fact to a realm-wide fact plus !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(); the skip is now denied to every user in a passkey-enabled realm, including those with no WebAuthn credential, forcing password-only users through an extra form render with no passkey option.

[ADVISORY] WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm (lines 100-128): the non-conditional fillContextForm behavior is silently narrowed so the user != null branch runs only when shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) returns true; the isUserIdentified flag semantics changed from 'user was set' to 'some subclass said show', so future callers on the conditional authenticator get isUserIdentified=false even when a user is present, rendering the wrong template variant.

[ADVISORY] New condition in UsernameForm.java:47 (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) makes the username form re-appear during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled, allowing the subject of the flow to be swapped by typing a different username, violating the re-authentication invariant for step-up flows (acr/step-up, broker re-auth, reauth-scoped auth sessions), with no feature flag for operators

[ADVISORY] In WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-107, fillContextForm gates the identified-user branch on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) and falls through to the unidentified branch (discoverable-credential usernameless challenge) when it returns false; the control-flow coupling is fragile, so any future non-conditional-UI subclass overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to false will silently lose the allowCredentials restriction, and the branch semantics are semantically overloaded by a method named only about display

[ADVISORY] PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses a broken webauthn-form-absence check: fail() is dead code since findElement never returns null, and catch (Exception) swallows non-absence Selenium failures, so the test passes for unintended reasons; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

[ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError has no test asserting its observable effects (username hidden, registration disabled); regression that drops the new WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse call site or reads the wrong auth-note key would pass the suite

[ADVISORY] The new guard in UsernameForm.java:47's negative path (conditional passkeys enabled, user set during re-auth, but user has no passkey credential or has linked brokers) is exercised by no test, leaving the behavior change unverified

[ADVISORY] The null-user boundary of the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled predicate in UsernamePasswordForm is untested: authenticate's moved fillContextForm block now requires user != null, so initial (non-re-auth) login no longer fills webauthn form data through this path with no test coverage distinguishing which code path rendered the form

[BUG] UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 (and :137): passkey-form setup gate inverted — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null, so on initial login render of combined UsernamePasswordForm flow when user is null, fillContextForm is no longer invoked in authenticate() or challenge(), causing first-visit users on a combined username+password page in a passkeys-enabled realm to get a page without WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes, silently missing the browser autocomplete passkey option and regressing initial-login conditional passkeys

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.java:47: new condition context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() unconditionally shows the username form during re-authentication whenever the realm's passkeys policy is enabled, without checking that the re-authenticating user actually owns any WebAuthn credential or linked broker — users without passkeys in passkey-enabled realms now hit an extra 'enter your username' step on every prompt=login re-authentication; fix should be a per-user credential check as fillContextForm's empty-bean path does

[ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.java:127: Boolean.parseBoolean(userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth) parses the raw auth note; any note value other than exact string 'true' (e.g. 'TRUE', '1', or user-controlled values from custom flows) silently yields false, causing the re-auth form to fall back to regular username+password layout with registration link shown and no error or log — custom authenticators writing USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH with non-canonical values (invited by the constant being made public in this diff) get a half-broken re-auth page

Also, the only shown duplicate hook is in `challenge(context, String error, String field)`, which is an error-render path; the diff does not show that `challenge(context, formData)` (the normal first-render path) performs fillContextForm, so the claimed guaranteed duplication/doubled per-render work is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:222 — badPasswordHandler now delegates to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError which reads the auth note inline, duplicating the isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth helper's predicate logic in the same class hierarchy, risking silent divergence between the two readers when the flag storage changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` removed the call to `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` and instead calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which re-implements the predicate by directly reading `context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH)` and `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`. This duplicates the flag-reading logic outside the original class/hierarchy (and even required making `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` public for static import), so if the storage/key/semantics change later, the helper and the util can silently diverge. This is a maintainability/architecture concern created by the change, not a directly verifiable functional bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate: the new !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() branch has no test assertion verifying which branch executed — PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication passes identically whether the username form was rendered or silently skipped, so a regression in the skip condition ships undetected; the test never asserts loginPage.assertCurrent() or presence/absence of the username field between the re-auth request and appPage.assertCurrent()

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new control-flow in `UsernameForm.authenticate` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). The newly added re-authentication test `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` goes straight from opening the prompt=login request to `appPage.assertCurrent()` without asserting whether the username form was shown/skipped (e.g., `loginPage.assertCurrent()` or checking presence/absence of the username field). Because the test only verifies that login succeeds via passkey, it does not specifically lock in the intended behavior of the new skip condition, so regressions in that branching could be missed even if the end-to-end login still succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Missing test coverage for re-authentication of a user with no passkey credential while realm passkeys policy is enabled — the only 'user without passkey' test sets WebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled to FALSE, so the case the UsernameForm change alters (passkeys enabled, context.getUser() != null, zero webauthn credentials) is never exercised; a password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm is forced back through a username form with unknown rendering state instead of skipping to the password step

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it no longer skips the username form during re-authentication when `context.getUser() != null` if `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). The added tests cover multiple re-authentication paths, but the only explicit “user without passkey” re-auth test (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`) sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it does not exercise the edge case where realm passkeys are enabled yet the current user has zero WebAuthn credentials. That gap is diff-grounded and nontrivial because the changed skip condition could alter the re-auth flow/rendering for password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate: inverting the gate from isPasskeysEnabled() to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) drops the first-factor (user == null) fillContextForm call, so combined username/password flows lose conditional-UI setup on the initial login page; no test asserts webauthn autocomplete/conditional-UI presence on the initial page where user is null, making a regression breaking first-login passkey login via the combined form invisible

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate(...)` the diff introduces a call to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). Within the provided diff, no such zero-arg method is added to `UsernameForm` or shown in its superclass, while a similarly named method is added only to the sibling `UsernamePasswordForm` (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`). Based on what’s visible in the diff, this new call is unresolved and would cause a compilation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Scope drift: the guard in UsernameForm now forces the username form to be shown during every re-authentication in passkeys-enabled realms, but no test exercises UsernameForm itself; the interplay of hasLinkedBrokers with the new condition has zero coverage, so regressions (e.g., broker re-auth users seeing an unexpected username form) ship silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new conditional behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it used to short-circuit when `context.getUser() != null`, but now only does so when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (i.e., in the passkeys-enabled case it will no longer skip the username form even if a user is already set, and the `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` exception still applies). The added/modified tests in this PR focus on `UsernamePasswordForm`/WebAuthn conditional UI and re-authentication flows, but none explicitly cover `UsernameForm`'s re-authentication path nor the interaction with `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` under the new condition. That’s a specific, diff-grounded gap in coverage rather than a directly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Parallel hand-maintained gating: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) in UsernamePasswordForm re-implements the passkeys-available check already owned by WebAuthnAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled(), and the no-arg variant in UsernameForm is a second divergent copy; future conditions must be updated in multiple places, risking drift between flows — the gate should live in one place per the single-source-of-truth rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows UsernamePasswordForm introducing a small helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` that *delegates* to `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` and adds `user != null` as an extra condition; it does not re-implement `isPasskeysEnabled()` logic. The finding also asserts a “no-arg variant in UsernameForm” is a second divergent copy, but the implementation of that method is not shown in this diff, so the claimed duplicated/competing gating across flows cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Naming/scope mismatch: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is documented for the username-password form error path but is also invoked on the WebAuthn conditional-UI error challenge, setting USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a form outside its specified contract, so template changes to USERNAME_HIDDEN will silently affect the webauthn error page

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)` added with a name/comment specific to “UsernamePasswordForm” error handling, but it is invoked not only from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` (password error path) but also from `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` (a WebAuthn conditional-UI error challenge). The helper sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` on `context.form()`, so its effects are not limited to the username/password form context. This is a real scope/naming/contract concern grounded in the diff, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Public-surface widening: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is changed from protected to public solely so a util class in a different package can read it, making an internal auth-note key part of the permanent public API and making future renames/restructuring a breaking change for out-of-tree subclasses

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens visibility of `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `protected static final` to `public static final` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, and `AuthenticatorUtils` (different package) then `static import`s and uses it (`setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`). This is a concrete API-surface increase done to share an auth-note key across packages, which can constrain future renames/restructuring; it’s an architectural/API stability concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Test smell in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest: the 'webauthn button not present' assertions use try/catch with fail() as control flow, swallowing any exception (including NoSuchElementException) as a pass; these assertions can pass for the wrong reason and mask regressions, and should use Assert.assertThrows which is already used elsewhere in the same PR

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the “webauthn button not available” checks use try/catch with fail() and catch a broad Exception. Since driver.findElement(...) never returns null (it returns an element or throws), the nullValue() assertion is ineffective, and the broad catch will treat any exception (not just NoSuchElementException) as a pass, potentially masking real regressions. Using Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) (as referenced in the finding and used elsewhere in the PR) would make the intent precise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.java:47 — skip condition now gates on realm passkey policy instead of the user's actual credentials; a user with no WebAuthn credential in a passkey-enabled realm re-authenticating regresses from 'skip to password' to 're-enter username', contradicting the re-auth UX contract (USERNAME_HIDDEN) this PR preserves, since WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm bails out early offering them nothing for the extra step

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate` from always skipping the username step when `context.getUser() != null` to skipping only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. That means in a passkeys-enabled scenario, even if the user is already identified (typical re-authentication), the flow will no longer skip the username form and will require an extra username interaction. Nothing in the shown diff indicates this gating is based on the user actually having WebAuthn credentials (contrast with `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, which can return early when no authenticators exist in identified-user scenarios), so the finding’s core regression (“re-auth user may be forced back to username entry just because passkeys are enabled”) is verifiable from the `UsernameForm` condition change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.java:132 — util package statically imports a constant from browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, inverting the dependency direction between the util layer and browser-authenticator layer; the constant was promoted from protected to public solely for this import, and the pattern will grow the public surface with every shared note name — the note name should live in (or be passed from) the util/contract layer both read

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthenticatorUtils` (util package) adding `import static org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;` and using it in `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`. To enable this, `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` was changed from `protected static final` to `public static final` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`. This is a concrete layering/architecture concern introduced by the change (util now depends on a browser authenticator constant and expands the public API just to share a note key), but it is not a direct functional defect in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.java:47 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments but the only definition added in the diff is the protected (UserModel user) overload in sibling class UsernamePasswordForm; if no zero-arg overload exists this does not compile, and if it does, the two same-named predicates in sibling classes with different semantics is a naming collision that will mislead future editors and enable copy-paste bugs with divergent null-user handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no args, but the diff does not show the full `UsernameForm` class (or its superclasses) to confirm whether a zero-arg method already exists. The only method added in the diff is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, but that alone does not prove a compile error or a naming-collision issue because an existing zero-arg overload could already be present elsewhere. Therefore the finding’s compile-break/naming-collision claim is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey — coverage gap: no test exercises re-authentication through the separate UsernameForm execution for a user with no WebAuthn credential while the realm has passkeys enabled, precisely the case whose behavior changed in UsernameForm.authenticate; future tweaks or regressions to the skip condition would pass CI while silently changing re-auth UX in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes re-authentication behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate` by adding `&& !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` to the "skip the form when user is re-authenticating" path. That means when `context.getUser() != null` during re-auth AND conditional passkeys are enabled, the username form will no longer be skipped (behavior changed). The added/modified tests cover re-authentication mostly in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (single combined form execution) and re-auth cases where the user *has* a passkey; `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` explicitly sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it does not exercise the changed skip condition when passkeys are enabled. There is no test shown that runs a flow with a separate `UsernameForm` execution for a user without WebAuthn credentials while realm passkeys are enabled, so a regression in this new condition could slip through CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (lines 113-116): the original code set up WebAuthn data on the initial login page when user was not selected, but the diff inverts this so fillContextForm is only called when the user is already selected; the conditional-UI autofill setup for the anonymous first page is silently reversed, so the first username/password page no longer emits conditional-UI WebAuthn attributes and users lose browser passkey autofill on the initial page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reverse when WebAuthn conditional-UI form context is populated in `UsernamePasswordForm`. Previously, `challenge(context, error, field)` explicitly called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only when `context.getUser() == null` and passkeys were enabled; after the change it calls it only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper requires `user != null`. Likewise in `authenticate()`, the call is now guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which also prevents filling the form when no user is selected. This is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff and can remove conditional-UI-related attributes from the initial anonymous username/password page, matching the finding’s claim about losing passkey autofill there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 197-207): a previously accepted assertion that passkeys must be hidden on the username/password page once the user is identified is flipped to require the webauth form present, reversing an accepted behavioral constraint without evidence the spec owner signed off.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly and intentionally changes behavior/tests to keep the WebAuthn/passkeys form available even when the username is already identified (e.g., PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey now asserts the webauth form is present; UsernamePasswordForm now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) i.e., user != null). The finding’s core criticism (“reversing an accepted behavioral constraint without evidence the spec owner signed off”) is not something that can be verified from the diff itself, and it does not show a defect—just an intentional behavioral change reflected in code and tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm (line 47): the re-auth skip condition changed from a per-user fact to a realm-wide fact plus !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(); the skip is now denied to every user in a passkey-enabled realm, including those with no WebAuthn credential, forcing password-only users through an extra form render with no passkey option.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the re-auth short-circuit in `UsernameForm.authenticate` changing from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }`, meaning some previously-skipped re-auth cases will now render the username form when conditional passkeys are enabled. However, the finding’s stronger claim that this is based on a purely realm-wide flag and impacts “every user … including those with no WebAuthn credential” is not verifiable from this diff because `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` implementation is not shown here, and whether passkey UI is actually absent for such users depends on downstream logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm (lines 100-128): the non-conditional fillContextForm behavior is silently narrowed so the user != null branch runs only when shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) returns true; the isUserIdentified flag semantics changed from 'user was set' to 'some subclass said show', so future callers on the conditional authenticator get isUserIdentified=false even when a user is present, rendering the wrong template variant.

adjudication.rationale: In WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm the branch that previously ran whenever context.getUser() != null is now gated by the overridable shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context). WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides this to always return false, so fillContextForm will skip the “user identified / authenticators bean” path even when a user is present, leaving any state derived from that branch (e.g., isUserIdentified and related form attributes) in its default state. The diff does not show how isUserIdentified is used later in the method/template, so the claim that it definitively renders the wrong template variant can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the change does couple “user identified” semantics to an overridable “show UI” decision, which is a concrete design/maintenance concern introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New condition in UsernameForm.java:47 (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) makes the username form re-appear during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled, allowing the subject of the flow to be swapped by typing a different username, violating the re-authentication invariant for step-up flows (acr/step-up, broker re-auth, reauth-scoped auth sessions), with no feature flag for operators

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate` to *not* short-circuit when `context.getUser() != null` if conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). Previously, a pre-set user (typical in re-auth/step-up) would skip the username form, preventing changing the subject. With the new condition, the username form can be shown even though a user is already identified, and nothing in this diff shows the username being forced/hidden on the initial username form (the new `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` only applies to username/password form error cases). This makes it plausible that re-auth flows can accept a different username, violating the re-auth invariant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100-107, fillContextForm gates the identified-user branch on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) and falls through to the unidentified branch (discoverable-credential usernameless challenge) when it returns false; the control-flow coupling is fragile, so any future non-conditional-UI subclass overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to false will silently lose the allowCredentials restriction, and the branch semantics are semantically overloaded by a method named only about display

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` from branching on `user != null` to branching on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (and adds an overridable method). `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` now overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to always return `false`, which means `fillContextForm` will take the “unidentified user” path even when `context.getUser()` is set. That is a real, diff-grounded control-flow coupling between a method named around “showing authenticators” and core logic selection inside `fillContextForm`, making future overrides risky/misleading. However, the finding’s claim about “silently lose the allowCredentials restriction” can’t be verified from this diff because the else-branch behavior isn’t shown here, so it’s not a provable concrete bug in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses a broken webauthn-form-absence check: fail() is dead code since findElement never returns null, and catch (Exception) swallows non-absence Selenium failures, so the test passes for unintended reasons; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the absence check is implemented as `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) {}`. As the finding notes, `findElement(...)` does not return null when missing; it throws (typically NoSuchElementException), so the `nullValue()` assertion and subsequent `fail()` are effectively unreachable on the “element absent” path. Additionally, catching broad `Exception` will treat other Selenium failures (e.g., stale element, invalid selector, etc.) as “expected absence,” potentially letting the test pass for unintended reasons. This is a test robustness issue, not a product correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError has no test asserting its observable effects (username hidden, registration disabled); regression that drops the new WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse call site or reads the wrong auth-note key would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` that conditionally sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the auth-note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`, and wires it into two call sites (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). While several new tests are added around re-authentication/passkeys flows, none in the diff explicitly asserts these specific observable form effects (username hidden / registration disabled) or that the correct auth-note key is consulted; the tests mainly assert presence of the webauthn form, info messages, and successful login events. Therefore, a regression that removes these call sites or misreads the auth-note could plausibly pass the current suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new guard in UsernameForm.java:47's negative path (conditional passkeys enabled, user set during re-auth, but user has no passkey credential or has linked brokers) is exercised by no test, leaving the behavior change unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, meaning re-authentication no longer skips the username form when conditional passkeys are enabled. The new/altered behavior for the opposite branch (user already set during re-auth but conditional passkeys enabled) is not specifically covered by the added tests: new tests exercise re-authentication with passkeys (discoverable/external keys) and a case where passkeys are disabled at realm level, but none in this diff asserts behavior when the re-authenticated user lacks a passkey credential or when `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` would affect the prior skip path. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for nontrivial logic rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The null-user boundary of the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled predicate in UsernamePasswordForm is untested: authenticate's moved fillContextForm block now requires user != null, so initial (non-re-auth) login no longer fills webauthn form data through this path with no test coverage distinguishing which code path rendered the form

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the null-user boundary/path is untested, but the diff adds/updates multiple blackbox UI tests that exercise the initial login page (where `context.getUser()` would typically be null) and assert the WebAuthn/passkeys form is present (e.g., `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey()` asserts `//form[@id='webauth']` exists right after `oauth.openLoginForm()`). So there is coverage that the initial (non-reauth) login still renders the WebAuthn UI, even if the internal `fillContextForm` call site changed. The assertion that there is "no test coverage" for this behavior is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] UsernamePasswordForm.java:113 (and :137): passkey-form setup gate inverted — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null, so on initial login render of combined UsernamePasswordForm flow when user is null, fillContextForm is no longer invoked in authenticate() or challenge(), causing first-visit users on a combined username+password page in a passkeys-enabled realm to get a page without WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes, silently missing the browser autocomplete passkey option and regressing initial-login conditional passkeys
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate reports that isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires a non-null user, so on the initial login render when context.getUser() is null, fillContextForm is not called in authenticate()/challenge(), preventing WebAuthn conditional UI setup and breaking first-time (ID-less) passkey login. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.java:47: new condition context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() unconditionally shows the username form during re-authentication whenever the realm's passkeys policy is enabled, without checking that the re-authenticating user actually owns any WebAuthn credential or linked broker — users without passkeys in passkey-enabled realms now hit an extra 'enter your username' step on every prompt=login re-authentication; fix should be a per-user credential check as fillContextForm's empty-bean path does

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`. This means that in realms where conditional passkeys are enabled, the previous re-auth optimization (skipping the username step when the user is already in the context and has no linked brokers) no longer applies, so the username form will be shown even for re-authenticated users who may not have any WebAuthn credentials. The finding’s suggestion (doing a per-user capability/credential check before forcing the username step) is grounded, but the diff does not show a clear correctness/security break—this looks like a UX/flow tradeoff made to support conditional passkeys rather than an outright defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils.java:127: Boolean.parseBoolean(userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth) parses the raw auth note; any note value other than exact string 'true' (e.g. 'TRUE', '1', or user-controlled values from custom flows) silently yields false, causing the re-auth form to fall back to regular username+password layout with registration link shown and no error or log — custom authenticators writing USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH with non-canonical values (invited by the constant being made public in this diff) get a half-broken re-auth page

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Boolean.parseBoolean(userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth)` in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`. In Java, `Boolean.parseBoolean` is case-insensitive (`"TRUE"` yields `true`), so the finding’s claim that anything other than exact string `'true'` (including `'TRUE'`) becomes false is incorrect. The rest (custom authenticators writing non-canonical values like `'1'`, user-controlled auth notes, and resulting “half-broken” pages) is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.
